plain.headline: Prepare the Way
plain.intro: Isaiah announces comfort to God's people: God is coming, so build a straight road for him through the desert. Peter explains that God's seeming delay is patience, giving everyone time to turn back to him. In the Gospel, John the Baptist takes up Isaiah's words, calls people to repentance, and points to one mightier than himself.
plain.listen: the voice crying out in the wilderness, in both Isaiah and the Gospel

Reading 1.box: God tells his prophet to comfort his people, because their time of punishment is over. A voice calls for a road through the desert so that God can come, and a messenger announces that God is coming with power and with a shepherd's tenderness. These words were first spoken to God's people living in exile in Babylon, far from home.

chunks.text: "Comfort, comfort my people," says your God. "Speak tenderly to Jerusalem. Tell her that her time of hardship is over and her sin is forgiven. She has received from the Lord's hand double for all her sins."

A voice calls out, "In the wilderness, prepare the way of the Lord. Make a straight, level road in the desert for our God. Every valley will be raised and every mountain and hill made low. Rough ground will become level and rugged places smooth. Then the Lord's glory will be revealed, and all people will see it together. The Lord himself has said it."

You who bring good news to Zion, climb a high mountain. You who bring good news to Jerusalem, shout it out with strength. Do not be afraid. Say to the towns of Judah, "Here is your God." Look, the Lord God is coming with power, and his arm rules for him. He brings his reward with him. Like a shepherd he will feed his flock. He will gather the lambs in his arms and carry them close to his heart. He will gently lead the mothers with their young.

Responsorial Psalm.box: The psalm promises that God speaks peace to his people and that his salvation is near. Mercy and truth meet, justice and peace embrace, and justice walks ahead of God to prepare his way.

Reading 2.box: Some Christians were asking why Jesus had not yet come back. Peter answers that God does not count time as we do, and that the delay is God's patience, giving everyone time to repent. The day will come without warning, so we should live holy lives as we wait for a new heaven and a new earth.

chunks.text: Dear friends, do not forget this one thing: with the Lord, one day is like a thousand years and a thousand years like one day. The Lord is not slow to keep his promise, as some people think. He is patient with you. He does not want anyone to be lost, but wants everyone to turn back to him.
But the day of the Lord will come like a thief. On that day the heavens will pass away with a roar, the elements will melt in the heat, and the earth and everything done on it will be burned up.

Since everything will come to an end this way, think what kind of people you should be. Live holy and godly lives as you wait for the day of God and long for it to come. On that day the heavens will be dissolved in fire and the elements will melt in the heat.

But we are waiting for what God promised: new heavens and a new earth, where justice is at home. So, dear friends, as you wait for these things, do all you can to be found at peace, spotless and blameless in his sight.

Gospel.box: Mark opens his Gospel with John the Baptist, the messenger the prophets promised. John lives simply in the desert and calls people to turn from their sins and be baptized. He says plainly that someone much greater is coming after him. Mark's Gospel begins here, with no story of Jesus' birth.

chunks.text: This is the beginning of the Good News of Jesus Christ, the Son of God. As the prophets wrote, "I am sending my messenger ahead of you to prepare your way. He is a voice shouting in the wilderness, 'Prepare the way of the Lord. Make his paths straight.'"

So John came into the wilderness, baptizing and preaching that people should turn from their sins and be baptized, so that their sins would be forgiven. People from all over Judea and everyone from Jerusalem went out to him. They confessed their sins, and he baptized them in the Jordan River.

John wore clothes made of camel's hair with a leather belt around his waist, and he ate locusts and wild honey. He announced, "Someone more powerful than I am is coming after me. I am not worthy to bend down and untie the straps of his sandals. I have baptized you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit."

plain.carry: This week I will clear one rough place in my life, a habit or a grudge, so there is a straighter road for Jesus to come to me.

kids.headline: Make a Path for Jesus
kids.intro: Today we meet John the Baptist, who helped people get ready for Jesus. The readings talk about making a smooth, straight road so God can come to his people.
kids.listen: the man who lives in the desert and eats locusts and wild honey

Reading 1.box: God tells the prophet Isaiah to comfort his people, who were far from home and sad. God is coming to them, so they should make a smooth road for him. When he comes, he will care for them like a shepherd.

chunks.text: God says, "Comfort my people. Speak kindly to them. Tell them their hard times are over and their sins are forgiven." A voice calls out, "Make a road for God in the desert. Fill in the valleys and flatten the hills. Make the bumpy places smooth. Then everyone will see how great God is."

Climb a high mountain and shout the good news. Do not be afraid. Say, "Here is your God." God is coming, strong and powerful. He will take care of his people like a shepherd. He will pick up the little lambs, hold them close, and gently lead the mother sheep.

Responsorial Psalm.box: This song says God is bringing peace to his people. When God is near, kindness and truth, goodness and peace all come together.

Reading 2.box: Saint Peter writes to Christians who were wondering why Jesus had not come back yet. He tells them God is patient because he wants everyone to come back to him. While we wait, we should live good and holy lives.

chunks.text: Do not forget: to God, one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day. God is not late in keeping his promise. He is being patient, because he wants everyone to turn back to him and no one to be lost. But the day of the Lord will come as a surprise, like a thief at night. The sky and the earth as we know them will pass away in fire.

So be holy and good while you wait for God's day, when this old world will melt away. God has promised a new heaven and a new earth, where everything is good and right. So, dear friends, while you wait, try your best to live in peace and do what is right, so God finds you ready.

Gospel.box: Mark's Gospel begins with John the Baptist. John lived in the desert and asked people to tell God they were sorry for their sins and to be baptized. He told them that someone much greater was coming soon, and that someone was Jesus.

chunks.text: This is the start of the Good News about Jesus Christ, the Son of God. Long ago the prophets said God would send a messenger to get people ready, a voice calling in the desert, "Get ready for the Lord. Make his paths straight." That messenger was John. He came to the desert, baptizing people and telling them to turn away from their sins so God would forgive them.

People came from everywhere to see him. They told God they were sorry for their sins, and John baptized them in the Jordan River. John wore clothes made of camel hair and a leather belt. He ate insects called locusts, and wild honey. He said, "Someone much greater than me is coming. I am not even good enough to untie his sandals. I baptize you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit."

word.meaning: To repent means to be truly sorry for doing wrong and to turn back to God, ready to do better.

kids.draw: Draw a bumpy, crooked road being made smooth and straight, with Jesus coming down the road.
kids.ask: What is one thing you could do this week to make your heart ready for Jesus?

family.opener: Today John the Baptist calls out in the desert, telling everyone to get ready because the Lord is coming.
questions: If our hearts were a road for Jesus, what bumps or crooked places might need fixing?
Why do you think so many people walked out into the desert to hear John?
Isaiah says God carries his lambs close to his heart. When have you felt God taking care of you?
family.try: Choose one thing that often causes trouble at home, like arguing over chores, and work on it together all week to make a smooth path for Jesus.
family.pray: Lord Jesus, help our family turn back to you and make our hearts a smooth, straight road for your coming.
